To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

3T3T mesenchymal cells express a defect in the control of their differentiation and proliferation and that this defect is associated with an increased proclivitity to undergo metaplasia, dedifferentiation and neoplasis.

predifferentiation growth-arrest and nonterminal differentiation of 3T3T mesenchymal cells is completely reversible, and that the dedifferentiated cells are capable of redifferentiating into adipocytes and macrophages.

the ability to undergo nonterminal differentiation and to undergo dedifferentiation and transdifferentiation is not limited by the process of differentiation in the 3T3T mesenchymal cell system, but is limited by neoplastic transformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether preneoplastic changes in cells are associated with the loss of their ability to regulate their proliferation and/or their differentiation.
the study of the molecular basis of the control of differentiation and growth in normal cells and in cells that have undergone preneoplastic and neoplastic transformation.
the molecular mechanisms of differentiation and the control of differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data support a model in which the early events of carcinogenesis are associated with the expression by the cells of defects in the integral control of cellular differentiation and proliferation and in the expression of the ability to undergo complete terminal differentiation.
the expression of defects that affect the integrality of cellular differentiation and proliferation are of etiological significance for the development of preneoplasias and neoplasias.
preneoplastic stem cells express an increased potential to undergo both neoplastic and metaplastic changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3T3 cells are not normal stem cells, but they are preneoplastic stem cells.
the 3T3T cells are preneoplastic, but they can undergo differentiation and dedifferentiation.

the data show that the expression of a stable program of nonterminal differentiation is not required for the cells to undergo complete dedifferentiation and that the expression of such a program is not required for subsequent redifferentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when a cell is in a state of dedifferentiation, it is more likely to undergo neoplasia than if it is in a state in which it has undergone nonterminal differentiation.
, if the preneoplastic state can be defined as one of increased differentiation potential, the preneoplasias of 3T3T cells are reversible.
, in the context of the 3T3 system, metaplasia does not necessarily lead to neoplasia, but that neoplasia is more likely in the presence of metaplasia.
